newsitem.title: USA: BOC Freedman promotes independent monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: BOC Freedman promotes independent monetary policy.

text.p: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Charles Freedman on Thursday said Canadian monetary policy should focus on domestic factors, despite an obvious need to consider developments in the U.S. economy.
Freedman was asked if the Bank of Canada should follow the Federal Reserve's move to boost U.S. interest rates two weeks ago with an increase of its own.

"Obviously Federal Reserve policy is important for Canada," Freedman said at a conference at the Jerome Levy Economics Institute. "That does not preclude a monetary policy that is focused on domestic factors."
Freedman cited increased confidence in Canadian fiscal policy as well as slower inflation than in the United States as signs that Canada was able to conduct monetary policy independent of Fed policy.
"We can have a monetary policy that does not move in lockstep with the U.S.," Freedman said.
Freedman declined further comment on monetary policy or on the Canadian dollar, which fell to a two-year low against the U.S. dollar on Thursday.
